div.l: Latte se who shall telle the furst tale
As so eủere mot y drynke wyne or ale
Who so be rebell to my Iugement
Shall paie for all that is by the wey spent
Nowe drawith Cutte or we ferther twyn̄
For he that hath the shortist shall be gyn̄
Sir knyght quod he my Master and my lorde
Nowe drawith Cut for this for this is myn̄ accorde
Comth nere quod . he my lady prioresse
And ye Sir Clerke let be youre shamfastnesse
Ne studieth nought ley hande to eủery man̄
And to drawe eủery wight began
And shortly to telle as it was
Were it by adventure or sorte or cas
The sothe is the Cutte felle to the knyght
Of which full gladde was eủery wyght
And tell he moste his tale as it was reasoıı̄un
By forward and by composicyoıı̄un
And that ye haue harde what nedeth wodes moo
And whan̄ this gode man̄ sawe it was soo
As he that wise was and obedient
To kepe his forward by his fre assent
And seide sith y shall begynne the game
Welcom̄ be the Cutte in goddis name
Now lette vs ride and herkenyth what y sey
Nowe with that worde we riden̄ furth on̄ oure wey
And he began̄ with right a mery chere
His tale anon̄ and seide on̄ this manere

Iamqꝫue domos patrias Scithice post asꝑpera gentes Prelia
laurigero ⁊etc̉etera
Explicit
Nowe begynneth the knyght his tale
Whilom̄ as olde stores tellen̄ vs
There was a Duke that hight Theseus
Of Athenes he was lorde and goủernoure
